description: Segmentation of the separated vocal of v2_2 (first AI take): 7 verses x 5 segments, cut points and fades for the 3 kept pieces per verse, syllables with pitch, the 'atları' check, the table of sung notes, noise floor.

source.timeline: all times are seconds on the timeline of the separated vocal = timeline of v2_2.mp3 decoded by ffmpeg (measured lag 0 samples)

levels.definition: RMS over the word intervals of the kept words (words file)

definitions.segments: L1, L2, ses (the two sung animal-sound words: REMOVE), diye ('diye bağırır'), L4. start / end from the vocal's own 10 ms RMS envelope.
definitions.pieces: the three chunks to keep per verse: 1 = L1, 2 = L2, 3 = diye + L4 (one continuous chunk). cut_in = instant where the fade-in starts (gain 0); the fade-in lasts fade_in_ms. cut_out = instant where the fade-out has reached 0; it starts fade_out_ms earlier. Raised-cosine fades.
definitions.placement: piece.placement.shift_s moves the piece from the source timeline to the new song form (no time-stretch; the source grid is 105.003 BPM, the new form 105.000 BPM: the difference is 0.06 ms per bar).
definitions.syllable.start/end: boundaries from the audio; kind / where of each boundary in end_boundary (see method.boundary_kinds).
definitions.syllable.kept / excise: excise = true only for the extra nucleus of verse 3 'atları' (to be cut out); every other syllable is kept.
definitions.syllable.f0_*: median over the syllable core (voiced frames within 6 dB of the 300-3400 Hz envelope peak); pyworld harvest, 5 ms.
definitions.syllable.pitch_start/mid/end: medians over the first quarter / middle half / last quarter of the core frames; is_glide if |end - start| >= 0.7 semitone.
definitions.syllable.notes: stable note plateaus inside the syllable (>= 40 ms within one semitone, slope <= 0.35 st per 20 ms); they partition the syllable in time.
definitions.syllable.voiced_ratio: share of the 5 ms frames of the syllable that are voiced (harvest) with the 100-1000 Hz envelope above sung RMS - 11 dB (the gate keeps the tracker's false pitches in fricatives and bursts out).
definitions.word.flag: true if (a) a boundary inside the word has no acoustic evidence and was placed on the beat grid, or (b) the sung syllables deviate from the lyric.
definitions.word.blind_check: independent count of envelope peaks without the grid; a mismatch is reported but is not by itself a flag (see syllable_scan.blind_count_note).

method.features: 10 ms and 5 ms RMS, band envelopes 100-1000 / 300-3400 / 1000-3400 / 4000-12000 Hz, log-mel flux, pyworld harvest f0 (cross-check dio+stonemask)
method.nuclei: expected vowel onsets from the beat grid template (izgara.py: every syllable sits on the sixteenth-note grid of the 105 BPM machine tempo); the nucleus is the envelope peak near the expected place. The self-trained letter HMM of the earlier take was tried and discarded (unreliable on this take).

boundary_kinds.dip / deepest: a dip of at least 3 dB in the 300-3400 Hz envelope (12 ms) between the two nuclei; the boundary is the centre of the dip (middle of the consonant / closure)
boundary_kinds.dip / last_low: coda + onset consonants: the last low region before the next syllable's onset
boundary_kinds.dip / closure_after_sonorant: coda n, m, l, r + stop onset (nın|bir, ğin|de, bir|çift, ör|dek, rır|çift): the closure, i.e. the lowest 5 ms RMS before the next vowel (for b, d only within -50 .. +30 ms of the expected vowel onset)
boundary_kinds.dip / voicing_onset: voiceless coda (t, k, ... , z) + liquid onset (çift|li, nek|le, roz|la): the instant voicing starts after the burst / frication
boundary_kinds.dip / fricative_onset: vowel + s (di|si): the instant the previous vowel ends
boundary_kinds.dip / glottal: vowel | vowel across a word boundary with a glottal dip of at least 4 dB (de|i, de|A)
boundary_kinds.spectral / nasal_release: nasal coda + liquid onset (yun|la): the instant the nasal ends (rise of the 1-3.4 kHz band / positive spectral flux)
boundary_kinds.spectral / glide_*: the y glide (ko|yun, di|ye): F2 peak or two-segment fit of the log-mel spectrum
boundary_kinds.spectral / two_segment_fit: no dip but different vowels (ba|ğı): the instant that best splits the log-mel spectrum into two constant parts
boundary_kinds.pitch_step: no dip and no spectral change (same vowel across 'ğ': li|ği) but the note changes: the instant f0 crosses the midpoint between the two notes
boundary_kinds.grid (FLAG): no acoustic mark at all (same vowel, same pitch: li|ğin; or a weak glide more than 70 ms off the grid: di|ye in two verses): the boundary is put on the expected beat-grid position of the next syllable and the word is flagged
boundary_kinds.splice: verse 3 'atları' only: end of the excision range inside the sustained l

method.hard_cut_a: end of 'var' = first instant after the vowel where the 1-3.4 kHz band has fallen 12 dB below its peak in the vowel and stays there >= 20 ms (cross-check: steepest 10 ms fall). What follows is classified from the next 50 ms: pause (>= 30 ms below sung RMS - 12 dB), nasal murmur (voiced, energy only below 1 kHz), fricative.
method.hard_cut_b: deepest point of the 10 ms RMS between the body of the second sung animal sound and the /d/ burst of 'diye'; the fade-in ends 2 ms before the level rises 6 dB above that dip.

atlari_check.verdict: FOUR syllable nuclei were sung (a - tı - la - rı), not three (at - la - rı): the user's impression 'atıları' is confirmed.
atlari_check.verdict_detail: After the /t/ release the voice re-enters 261 ms before the 'a' of 'la'. That stretch is its own note (E4 on beat 6.5, like the second syllable of the four-syllable animal words): a short bright vowel-like part (82 ms, -18.5 dBFS RMS; the two 'a' vowels of the word: -18.9 and -18.1 dBFS) followed by a sustained dark /l/ (180 ms). In the other consonant + l + vowel words the voiced part before the vowel lasts 6-50 ms (median 32 ms, n = 24).

spectral_evidence.measure: spectral envelope sampled at 350 ... 2800 Hz (interpolated between the harmonic peaks, dB re strongest, floor -35 dB); RMS distance in dB to the mean envelope of each class, using only reference sounds of the same singer within +-1.5 semitones (verse 3 'atları' excluded from the references)
spectral_evidence.note: f0 is 330-350 Hz, so the envelope is only visible at the harmonics and LPC formants lock onto them: the harmonic levels are the main evidence

excision.start_definition: quietest instant between the end of the /t/ frication and the onset of voicing (5 ms RMS -39.7 dBFS)
excision.end_definition: 55 ms before the onset of the 'a' of 'la' (F2-band rise): keeps a normal-length /l/ in front of 'a'

recommended_fades.note: the splice-in point lies inside the sustained /l/ (voiced, about -21 dBFS): a 10 ms fade-in is needed

minimal_alternative.note: removes only the bright vowel-like part and keeps the whole sustained /l/ (180 ms on E4): NOT recommended, a sustained l on its own note still reads as a syllable ('atılları')

rhythm_options.what: leave a gap: every remaining sample stays at its original time
rhythm_options.result: 'at' on beat 6 (vowel 162 ms + /t/ closure and release), rest on beat 6.5, 'la' on beat 7, 'rı' on beat 7.25, 'var' on beat 7.5 as sung

rhythm_options.what: close the gap by moving 'ları var' earlier
rhythm_options.result: 'var' would land 0.37 beats before its beat (off the grid) and line 2 would end 212 ms early: not recommended

rhythm_options.what: close the gap by moving 'at' later

atlari_check.not_verified_by_ear: The verdict rests on measurements (timing, level, spectrum, pitch). Whether the repaired word sounds natural was not checked by listening.

syllable_scan.method: For every kept word, against the EXPECTED syllable list: (1) missing syllable = an expected syllable without a voiced nucleus at its beat-grid slot (less than 40 ms voiced or a core shorter than 30 ms); (2) extra syllable = two separate vowel peaks inside the interval of ONE expected syllable (vowel-like frames: voiced, 1-3.4 kHz band within 10 dB of the interval maximum and 4-12 kHz band above -55 dBFS; two runs of >= 40 ms separated by >= 30 ms of voiced sound in which the 1-3.4 kHz band drops >= 8 dB, i.e. vowel - sonorant consonant - vowel); (3) blind envelope peak count (no grid) as an independent cross-check; (4) syllable durations of the repeated words across the 7 verses.
syllable_scan.blind_count_note: A blind mismatch alone is not an error: 'li-ği' / 'li-ğin' are one continuous vowel (no dip), and a soft /l/, /n/ or /y/ between vowels often makes no 3 dB dip. These words were NOT split proportionally; the nuclei were anchored on the beat grid and the boundaries found acoustically.

notes_table.about: Sung notes measured on the separated vocal (kept syllables only; the sung animal sounds and the excised extra nucleus of verse 3 are not included). Durations in beats of the measured grid (0.5714133 s). A note lasts from its start to the start of the next note / end of the syllable (consonants included).
notes_table.pitch_outliers_note: kept syllables whose core pitch differs by 0.5 semitone or more from the median of the same template slot over the 7 verses
notes_table.histogram_note: duration-weighted: 5 ms frames, gated (voiced, 100-1000 Hz envelope above sung RMS - 11 dB), summed over the 7 verses. 'stable_notes' counts only frames inside note plateaus (glides between notes excluded); 'per_beat' is for the bar of each line (diye: beats 2-3 of its bar), stable frames only.

noise_floor.between_verses_definition: instrumental stretches of the stem: from 0.25 s after the end of line 4 (after-sound included) to 0.65 s before the next verse (the breath before the verse is left out); this is what the separator left of the old band
noise_floor.note: The stem is NOT digitally silent between segments. Inside the phrases the stop closures sit around the stated median; the cut points of the kept pieces are listed per verse. Only the join 'var' -> sung animal sound has no low point at all in verses with /m/ or /h/ (see hard_cuts.L2_end).

grid_check.about: syllable start (boundary found on the audio) minus the expected vowel onset on the beat grid, per template slot, over the 7 verses. Negative = the syllable (its consonant) starts before the beat, as it should; a constant, narrow range confirms the template.

not_verified_by_ear: Nothing in this file was checked by listening.
